nodes.question: Compared with the source image, is there clear visible evidence that the same woman's jacket front closure has moved toward closing in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the closure itself is visible enough to compare and shows progress toward bringing the front panels together, even if an opening remains. Fail only when the closure is clearly assessable and shows no progress or is more open. Unknown when the turned pose, drape, or occlusion prevents reliable comparison; do not infer progress or its absence from silhouette alone.
nodes.binding: Compare the same jacket's front closure in the source and edited images. Judge actual alignment or separation along the closure, not the woman's pose or the jacket's outward flare. This is a progress check, not a full-closure check.

nodes.question: In the edited image, is the same woman's jacket fully closed, with no visible opening remaining along its front closure?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the visible closure itself shows the panels meeting with no opening. Fail only if an opening along the closure is clearly visible; panels appearing separated solely because the jacket flares with the turned pose is not sufficient. Unknown if pose, drape, or occlusion prevents judging the closure itself.
nodes.binding: Assess the same woman's jacket. Inspect the edited image's front closure, distinguishing a visible opening along the closure from outward flare or silhouette caused by pose and drape. Full closure is required; partial closure is not complete fulfillment. Use the source only to identify the garment, not to infer the edited endpoint.

nodes.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed?
nodes.criteria: Complete only when s2 passes and s1 passes, establishing both full closure and visible progress relative to the source. Partial only when s1 passes and s2 fails, establishing progress with a remaining opening. Absent only when s1 fails and s2 fails, establishing no progress and an incomplete endpoint. Unknown whenever either required observation is unknown, or when s2 passes but s1 does not pass; do not infer progress from endpoint closure alone or infer no progress from s2 failure alone. Use only the saved support observations.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment composition is incomplete: it can return complete when s2 passes, but it has no rule for combining s1 pass (evidence of progress) with s2 fail (visible remaining opening). That case establishes progress and incompleteness and must be partial, not merely partial without regard to s1 or unresolved. The saved criteria instead say s2 fail is partial without asserting progress, which conflicts with the rubric’s requirement that partial means some requested change has progressed. Thus the readout cannot faithfully distinguish progress from no progress when the jacket remains open.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment rule is contradictory for the case s1=pass and s2=pass: it says complete only when s2 passes, but also defines partial when s1 passes and s2 fails without explicitly making the complete case exclusive; more importantly, s1 can pass while s2 passes even if the edited jacket was already fully closed in the source, so the program can credit completion without evidence that the requested change progressed. The full-closure check is endpoint-only and explicitly uses the source only to identify the garment. It therefore needs evidence that the requested closure change occurred, or a rule that treats an already-closed source as requiring no change.
